llm_proposer.assessment: The fault localizes to the S05 launch into OMS S05→S09, before booster amp0. The approximately 6 dB drop is already present at amp0 input, propagates through every amplifier and channel monitor, and degrades och41 at S04; unchanged pump currents and downstream amplifier gains argue against an amplifier-originated fault.

proposals.rationale: A disturbed or partially disconnected S05→S09 OMS input patch best explains the simultaneous all-channel power reduction at amp0 input and throughout the section, with recent maintenance at S05 adding support. The documented mode normally causes complete signal loss rather than the observed persistent 6 dB reduction, so the fit is not exact.

Added loss can produce the observed persistent, common-channel power and OSNR degradation. However, loss in the span preceding amp1 would not explain why amp0 input and output had already fallen by the same amount, placing the origin earlier than that span.

A common S05 WSS port problem could affect multiple channels launched toward S09 and is consistent with the localization before amp0. A documented port failure should block the channels completely, whereas substantial optical power remains.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A booster gain problem could lower downstream power and OSNR. It is unlikely because amp0 output follows its already-reduced input almost one-for-one, while pump current is unchanged, indicating preserved gain rather than a gain drop.

proposals.rationale: Receiver degradation at the S04 end of och41 could explain its estimated-OSNR and pre-FEC BER changes. It cannot explain the independently measured all-channel power and OSNR reductions beginning on S05→S09, so it is unlikely to be the root cause.
